intro: Tax preparers work carefully with numbers, rules and clients, skills used across bookkeeping, payroll and benefits work. The closest of the 25 careers below is bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerk work, with a 95% match, while Brokerage Clerks are 91% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $65,750, or 20% more.
why_it_works: Tax season means interviewing clients, finding every deduction they qualify for and filing accurate returns on deadline. O*NET rates time management at 3.12 out of 5 for this job, and service orientation and judgment at 3. Bookkeeping, payroll and claims work use the same accuracy. Most matches need no new degree. The gaps are operations monitoring and managing people.
tips: Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks earn $58,260, which is 6% more, and work year-round.
Claims adjusters earn $78,000, or 42% more, and use your rule-reading skills.
An enrolled agent credential lets you represent clients before the IRS and raises your rates.

faq.q: What jobs can former tax preparers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks (95%), Brokerage Clerks (91%) and loan interviewers and clerks (87%), based on O*NET 31.0. Payroll and timekeeping clerks are 85% matched and earn $58,260, which is 6% more than the $54,920 tax preparer median.

faq.q: Which careers for tax preparers pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Financial Managers earn $166,570 (203% more), compensation and benefits specialists $78,210 (42% more) and claims adjusters and examiners $78,000 (42% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. The first two usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Do tax preparers need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than tax preparers already have, including 9 of the top 10. In the closest match, 41% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and many bookkeeping roles train new staff on the job.

faq.q: What skills should tax preparers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, managing people, programming and managing materials. Judgment already rates 3 out of 5 for tax preparers in O*NET, so spreadsheet automation and supervising staff are the main steps toward better-paid finance roles.
